root_cause: Segment._split_cells guesses a start index proportionally, pos = int(cut/cell_length*len(text)) - 1, then only walks FORWARD. When double-width (CJK) characters sit early and single-width ones later, the guess can already be past the cut (verified: 'メルク (CV: 水瀬いのり)     ' at cut=21 gives pos=14 with cell_len(text[:14])=22). The forward loop then immediately sees cell_pos > cut and returns a left segment that is one cell too wide (the test fails with 'assert 22 == 21').
best_solution: Keep the proportional guess (without the -1) but make the search go both ways: loop { before=text[:pos]; out_by=cell_len(before)-cut; if 0 -> return (before, text[pos:]); if out_by==-1 and text[pos] is double-width -> the cut falls inside text[pos], so return (text[:pos]+' ', ' '+text[pos+1:]); if out_by==+1 and text[pos-1] is double-width -> return (text[:pos-1]+' ', ' '+text[pos:]); else pos += 1 if under the cut, pos -= 1 if over }. Each branch keeps cell_len(left)==cut and cell_len(right)==total-cut. A plain linear scan from pos=0 is also correct, just slower.
acceptable_alternatives: Starting the scan at pos=0 (drop the proportional guess) passes all hidden tests (this is what p_v6 did). Clamping the guess backwards until cell_len(text[:pos]) <= cut before the forward loop is also correct.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_segment.py::test_split_cells_mixed is parametrized over 8 Japanese/mixed-width strings (e.g. 'メルク (CV: 水瀬いのり)     ', '南無阿弥JKうらめしや?！     ', 'メイド・イン・きゅんクチュアリ☆    ') and for every position in range(0, cell_length+1) asserts cell_len(left.text)==position and cell_len(right.text)==cell_length-position. No new API; existing split_cells semantics (a halved double-width char becomes two spaces) must hold.
locating_signals: Title names the function: 'Segment.split_cells fix' -> rich/segment.py Segment.split_cells/_split_cells. Body is only a link to a Textual issue (not provided to the agent) about double-width characters measured wrongly. The bug itself is not described; the agent has to write a brute-force check (every cut position on a CJK string) to find it.
our_outcome_summary: Only v6 passed (34s, 12 calls): it replaced the proportional start with pos=0 / cell_pos=0, a slower linear scan that is always correct. v4 failed (91s, 27 calls): it kept the overshooting start guess and only changed how a split double-width char is padded (split_before/split_after spaces), so 4 of the 8 parametrized cases still returned a left side one cell too wide ('assert 22 == 21'). v8 failed (62s, 29 calls): a cosmetic refactor (inlined `before`), no change in behavior. v7 produced an empty patch.
generalizable_lesson: When the statement is just 'fix function X' with a link you cannot see, write a brute-force property check first: call X on adversarial inputs (mixed-width or unicode text, edges 0 and len, every index) and assert its invariant (here len(left)+len(right) and left==cut). Then read every 'fast-path guess plus one-directional scan' for the case where the guess starts past the target. Don't patch the output-formatting branch until the check reproduces the failure, and treat a patch that only renames or refactors as no fix.
